clue.text: Artificial tooth I intend to put in mount

indicators.note: to put in tells us one piece is placed inside the abbreviation for mount

parts.note: Mt is the standard abbreviation for mount, as in Mt Everest
to intend something is to plan it

explanation.surface: Someone at the dentist resolves to have a false tooth fitted into its setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental implant is an artificial tooth anchored into the jawbone.

clue.text: 16, perhaps, investing leg in walk

indicators.note: investing in its old sense of clothing or surrounding, so the walk wraps round the leg

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON

explanation.surface: A queen, perhaps, is dressed up during a stately walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is QUEEN; a queen is one kind of sovereign ruler, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is an example of a sovereign ruler, which the defining word names generally.

clue.text: Cold fish comes up with hot sponge

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the cold fish reads from bottom to top

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
an eel is a snakelike fish
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An unfriendly person turns up with a warm bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns C plus EEL into LEEC; 'Cold fish' looks like an unfeeling person but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is a parasite who lives off others, exactly what a bloodsucking worm stands for.

clue.text: Remedy anything but alcohol, sucker initially swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means the first letter of sucker goes down inside the other piece

parts.note: anything but alcohol read playfully as 'not rum', any drink except a spirit

indicators.note: initially picks just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A teetotal cure: drink anything but alcohol, the gullible sucking it down first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anything but alcohol' is read as NOT RUM; S from 'sucker initially' goes inside after NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet remedy, often a quack medicine of doubtful worth.

clue.text: I'm surprised a soldier will retreat, as brave

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

explanation.surface: Astonishment that a soldier would fall back, as courageous as he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' is a noun here, a Native American warrior, not the adjective the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a North American Indian warrior, and the Arapaho are a Plains people.

clue.text: Haphazard money order

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A careless postal order for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard has no plan or pattern, the same idea as chance selection.

clue.text: Intrinsically charming to harass

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, intrinsically
cute means charming or appealing

explanation.surface: Being charming by nature is somehow a form of bullying.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute someone is to harass or hound them relentlessly.

clue.text: Pawn, male only entertained by tool

indicators.note: being entertained by a host means being held inside, so the stag goes inside the tool

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool
a stag party or stag night is for men only

explanation.surface: In chess, a lowly pawn and a man alone are hosted by a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' sounds like the chess piece of the theme, but it means someone held as a bargaining chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is a person used by others for their own ends, as a captive held for ransom is.

clue.text: Prude who stood out biting boy's bottom during functions

indicators.note: during means the rest of the wordplay sits within the word for functions

parts.note: a machine that functions goes, as in 'the engine goes'

indicators.note: biting means the anagram holds the letter between its teeth
out signals the letters of who stood rearranged
bottom picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prim person who made a spectacle, nipping a lad on the backside at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WHO STOOD into ODTWOSHO; 'biting' puts Y, the last letter of 'boy's' from 'bottom', after OD; 'during' places that inside GO...ES.
explanation.definitionFit: A goody two-shoes is a smugly virtuous person, close to a prude in showy propriety.

clue.text: 16, details to attach

indicators.note: read as de-tails, removing the tail or final letter of the word

parts.note: to annex something is to attach or append it

explanation.surface: A queen's paperwork is attached as a list of details.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is QUEEN; Queen Anne reigned over Britain from 1702 to 1714. 'details' is read as de-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was a British monarch, a queen regnant in the early eighteenth century.

clue.text: Having read a book, take a bird upstairs, perhaps, for an exchange of words?

definitions.text: Having read a book, take a bird upstairs, perhaps, for an exchange of words?

parts.words: Having read a book, take a bird upstairs, perhaps, for an exchange of words?
parts.note: swap the opening sounds of read a book to get bed a rook, that is, take a bird upstairs; such a swap is named after Dr Spooner

explanation.surface: A bedtime routine: finish reading, then carry a pet bird up to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates its answer: 'read a book' with initial sounds swapped is 'bed a rook', taking a bird upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping initial sounds of two words is the slip named after the Oxford don William Spooner.

clue.text: King, king after a day

indicators.note: after places the king letter following the a

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
Thur is an abbreviation of Thursday

explanation.surface: One king coming after another on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: R follows A, then the day completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur is the legendary British king of Camelot.

clue.text: Bishop is deacon after conversion

indicators.note: conversion changes the form of something, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A deacon becomes a bishop once he converts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' as a noun is defined by an adjective used as a noun: a diocesan is the bishop of a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese, as opposed to a suffragan.

clue.text: So there's no more moving ally in Havel, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: Vaclav Havel was the Czech president, so an ally of his could be a Czech mate

explanation.surface: Asking whether a friend of Havel ended the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Vaclav Havel was a Czech playwright and president; a pal of his would be a Czech mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate ends a chess game: the king is trapped and no further move can save it.

clue.text: Fake a shade below a king, for the most part

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the shade after the king
for the most part means only most of the king's name is used, its ending dropped

parts.note: Charles is the name of several English kings
tan is a light brown shade

explanation.surface: A bogus colour sits under a monarch, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud or impostor, a fake.

clue.text: One of four cards in group

definitions.meaning: a pack of playing cards holds four ..., one per suit
The British rock group fronted by Freddie Mercury

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack has four queens, and Queen was a famous rock band.

clue.text: Rook, bird eating larvae, ultimately

indicators.note: eating means the bird takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rook is a bird that eats grubs in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like a bird or the chess piece; here it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, to cheat.

clue.text: With opener dismissed, subject bagging duck on the rise, finding bottom edge

indicators.note: bagging means holding something inside, as in a bag
dismissing the opener, as in cricket, removes the first letter

parts.note: a theme is a subject

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so the word reverses

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, nil

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the opening batsman out, a duck rising, the side found at rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a cricket collapse; 'With opener dismissed', 'on the rise' and 'bagging' are the working words, and 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline is the lower edge of a skirt or dress.

clue.text: 16, perhaps, clue concealing complete lie, in conclusion

indicators.note: concealing means the clue word hides the other pieces inside

parts.note: a sign is a clue or indication
over means finished or complete

indicators.note: in conclusion picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A queen, perhaps, whose hint hides a total falsehood at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is QUEEN, one example of the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is an example of a sovereign, a supreme ruler.

clue.text: Pass old island

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-wife
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: A former island is handed on.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass waste from the body is to excrete it.

clue.text: Knight, given competition, 17-ed

parts.note: a gala is a sporting competition, such as a swimming gala
17 is CHEAT, so cheated means had, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: A knight entered a tournament and was cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Galahad was the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Offender in the main getting good price

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
a rate is a price, as in the going rate

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker mostly takes a fair price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, so an offender on the main is a sea robber; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate commits robbery on the high seas, the poetic 'main'.

clue.text: Quite insignificant accident, nursing bad back

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the accident holds the other piece

parts.note: a smash is a crash or accident

indicators.note: back means the word reads in reverse

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A minor crash, while tending an injured back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite insignificant' reads as describing the accident, but it is the definition; 'back' and 'nursing' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallish means fairly small, which is to say not very significant.

clue.text: Rook from herd, third one back

indicators.note: the third letter moves one step back in the alphabet, from T to the letter before it

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: A rook taken from a herd, the third one at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third one back' changes the third letter of CATTLE to the one before it in the alphabet, T to S.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the rook is also called the castle, from its turret shape.

clue.text: Rude chess player of diminished stature

definitions.meaning: curt or abrupt, as in being ... with someone
Nigel ... is an English chess grandmaster

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: Nigel Short challenged Kasparov for the world title in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Short means curt, small in height, and is the surname of the English grandmaster Nigel Short.

clue.text: Asian government council? Not so! Title's English

indicators.note: not so tells us to remove those two letters from the council word

parts.note: a soviet is a governing council in the former USSR
a title is a name; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Is that an Asian government council? No, its title is English.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnamese means from Vietnam, a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Line drawn in pub, no cheap drinks

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the words swallow the answer within them

explanation.surface: A pub line: no cut-price drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts the oche is the line players stand behind to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the throwing line in a game of darts, often played in pubs.

clue.text: Prince Philip's possible autobiography, wind!

definitions.meaning: Philip might title his memoir '...', the Queen being 'er
to wind is to twist and turn like a river

explanation.walkthrough: Prince Philip was the Queen's husband; his life story could be called 'Me and 'Er', dropped h and all.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wind along a twisting course, like a river.

clue.text: Roman defence trial, Japanese fighting to dispense with leader

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: dispensing with the leader removes the opening letter

parts.note: judo is a Japanese martial art

explanation.surface: A trial of Japanese combat that drops its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The testudo was a Roman formation where soldiers locked shields overhead like a tortoise shell.
